tweet_summary: Joel Berry (Babylon Bee writer) tweets a meme-format jab at Tucker Carlson with a photo of him examining a loaf of bread, claiming the bread 'costs the average Russian worker 3 days wages'.
why_note_decision: Although phrased as a joke meme ('find someone who looks at you the way...'), the embedded factual claim ('3 days wages for a loaf of bread in Russia') is concrete, viral, and false by roughly two orders of magnitude. A loaf costs ~50-65 RUB; average monthly Russian wage is ~100,000 RUB, so daily wage is ~3,000-4,000 RUB. Bread is ~1-2% of a day's wage, not 3 days. The author is a well-known commentator with 176K followers; the post has 4K likes and 128K impressions; commenters are confused ('how is anyone alive', 'must have a phd in stupidity to believe this'). The original note's facts are correct but it's poorly written ('Claim that the loaf equals three days' wages is false. A 1 lb loaf...'), uses awkward sourcing (numbeo + tradingeconomics), and many raters flagged it noteNotNeeded — probably because the tweet's meme framing made them treat it as obvious satire. But the comment section shows people are genuinely confused, so a clearer note IS warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS criteria: (1) Note must clearly state the '3 days wages' claim is false by a large margin. (2) Must give concrete numbers: a loaf of bread in Russia costs ~50-65 RUB; average daily wage is ~3,000+ RUB (monthly ~100,000 RUB), so bread is ~1-2% of a day's wage, not multiple days'. (3) Should be written plainly enough that a confused reader gets it on first read. FAIL if the note repeats the false framing ('costs 3 days' wages'), if it dodges by saying 'depends on region', or if it's so awkwardly worded that the correction is hard to extract. The bot should NOT decline this one — the meme framing isn't enough cover for a viral falsehood that confused commenters.
reference_note: False — bread costs a small fraction of a day's wage in Russia, not 3 days. A loaf typically runs ~50–65 RUB while average wages are ~3,000–4,000 RUB per day (~100,000 RUB/month). https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/country_result.jsp?country=Russia https://tradingeconomics.com/russia/wages

original_unhelpful_note.text: Claim that the loaf equals three days' wages is false. A 1 lb loaf in Russia costs ~50–65 RUB while average monthly wages are ~92,000 RUB, so bread is a tiny fraction of a day's pay, not multiple days' wages. https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/country_result.jsp?country=Russia https://tradingeconomics.com/russia/wages
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Hard-to-understand phrasing ('Claim that the loaf equals three days' wages is false') and weak sourcing for a viral claim. Substance is correct but execution led raters to mostly tag noteNotNeeded — perhaps because the awkward writing made it feel like sealioning a joke.

fact_check.claim_verdict: False — bread is a small fraction (~1-2%) of a Russian daily wage, not 3 days' wages.
fact_check.notes: Average gross monthly wage Russia 2025: ~100,000 RUB (~$1,034). Bread loaf 20-65 RUB. Even at minimum wage (~900 RUB/day), bread is well under a day's pay.

importance.lens_rationale: Viral economic disinfo about Russia from a high-follower account; correcting matters for accurate public perception of geopolitical/economic reality.
